meta.name: System Blueprint
meta.description: Map a Node.js repository's packages, runtime boundaries and state ownership.

nodes.title: Survey the system
nodes.description: Find modules, boundaries and sources of truth.
nodes.prompt: Start a structural system map for the Node.js repository requested by the user. Resolve the target from the request, Git roots, package.json and workspace manifests; the session may contain multiple repositories or a monorepo. If ambiguous, ask which target to review. Record session root, repo/package roots, branch, HEAD, dirty files, requested scope and budget. Read applicable instructions, README, package scripts and relevant established decisions. Choose a new report directory under docs/reviews/system-blueprint/ at the session project root, named <repo directory>-<UTC timestamp>-<short unique suffix>, or use the user's requested location. Never place it inside the reviewed repository or any other repository directory of the session: the workflow engine commits files a step writes onto that repository's checked-out branch, so a report there ships with the next pull request. If the session root is itself inside the reviewed repository (an app at the workspace root), use dazl-qa/reviews/system-blueprint/ instead, which Dazl keeps out of Git. Preserve existing reports and reuse this directory on retries. Record its session-relative path in inventory.md and in the handoff. QL is unavailable; use built-in search and source reads. Inventory the actual workspaces/packages and source areas, entrypoints, tests, build/runtime configuration, scripts, CI, deployment and relevant docs. Identify framework and module system from evidence. Group every area into an owner/domain with traced, sampled or unreviewed coverage; do not assume src/, app/, a frontend, a database or an HTTP server exists. Trace representative boundaries between packages/processes, handlers/services, state stores and external systems that actually exist. Mark inaccessible external internals unverified. If a subsystem was requested, limit inventory to it and direct boundaries. Write inventory.md with the structural map, representative crossing traces, source evidence and unknowns. Distinguish in-process imports/calls from network or queue communication and persistent state from caches. This is a structural map; only report defects supported by the inspected scope.

nodes.title: Draw the blueprint
nodes.description: Show module ownership and data movement.
nodes.prompt: Read inventory.md and draft report.md with a concise system overview, Mermaid context and package/ownership maps, and the main data/runtime boundaries. Ground calls, transports and stores in source; an import does not prove a runtime call. Add implemented design choices, documented or explicitly inferred rationale and tradeoffs. Include only systems actually present and retain coverage and unverified boundaries.

nodes.title: Verify the blueprint
nodes.description: Check the map against the implementation.
nodes.prompt: Verify and finish the System Blueprint structural map in report.md in the established report directory. Read the artifacts named by earlier stages and resolve material doubts with targeted source reads. Check findings, important diagram edges, source links, coverage and ownership. Validate Mermaid with already-installed tooling if available and report syntax/visual validation separately. Run a focused existing check only when it resolves a material claim; follow the target repo's test guidance and avoid full suites by default. Recheck application-code drift and record which revision/checks support the report; the report files live outside the reviewed repository and are never part of its code. Repair the report without changing application code. Include gaps, checks actually run, prioritized next actions, and the least-confident conclusion with its next check. Mark incomplete requested coverage explicitly. Finish with write_workflow_output pointing to report.md and a concise summary; report tokens only when measured. The input artifacts are inventory.md and report.md; boundary traces are in inventory.md, and no separate traces.md is required.
